info.title: Droppen Hub API
info.description: The hub's public API: accounts, devices, the chain, mail, the keyring, relays and pairings. The operator API (`/v1/admin/*`) is not part of this document.

delete.description:
`DELETE /v1/devices/{id}` → `204`: a current full device revokes a device
registered with the password alone that never joined the chain (#4: the
devices page lists the waiting ones, each with one tap to revoke it) —
its place in the day's registrations given back ([`db::register_device`])
— through [`revoke_waiting_device`]. `204` for one revoked already;
`403 not_a_full_device`; `404 not_found` for no device of the account;
`409 in_chain` for one the chain names in any state (removed through the
chain), `409 host_device` for a host's own row.

post.description:
`POST /v1/passkeys {challenge, label?, credential}` → the passkey's row
([`view`]): checked like a sign-up's (§3.4's table) against the challenge
this device was given for this account (after its proof, [`add_options`]);
then the account's daily share of additions, its cap, and the passkey
stored under its user handle. A refused credential is `400 bad_passkey`.
A current full device.

post.description:
`POST /v1/passkeys/add/options {current_password? | passkey?}` →
`{challenge, options}`: once it is proved still the person
([`reauthenticate`]: a passkey of the account's, or its current
password), a challenge bound to the account and this device, and creation
options under the account's user handle with its passkeys excluded.
Without that proof a browser left signed in could add a passkey of
someone else's — and with it set any password. Nothing is stored but the
user handle, the first time. A current full device.

default.description: `error` is the code, `message` a sentence; some codes add fields below.

post.description:
`POST /v1/passkeys/options {purpose: "signup", …}`: everything sign-up
checks, then a challenge bound to the e-mail and the creation options.
Nothing is stored. (Adding a passkey to an account takes a device
session: [`add_options`].)

**Whether the e-mail is taken is not said here** (pre-launch review):
it used to be, `409 email_taken` before any passkey existed, which made
this the cheapest way to ask the hub whether an address has an account —
one attempt from the address's share, no account made, no mail sent, no
trace for the address's owner. Now it answers a taken e-mail as any
other, and [`signup`] says `409 email_taken` where the password sign-up
does: when the account would be made, with a passkey made and verified
first, and the challenge spent. The cost: a person signing up with a
taken e-mail is left a passkey for no account in their authenticator.

default.description: `error` is the code, `message` a sentence; some codes add fields below.

post.description:
`POST /v1/passkeys/reauth/options {}` → `{challenge, options}`: a
challenge bound to the account and this device for proving it is still
the person ([`Purpose::Reauth`]: never a login's), and request options
naming the account's own passkeys. Nothing is stored. A current full
device of an account with a passkey (`409 no_passkey`: give the current
password instead) — or any of its devices before the account has a chain
(deleting it, `DELETE /v1/account`). Its e-mail need not be verified: what
the proof is for checks that itself.

default.description: `error` is the code, `message` a sentence; some codes add fields below.

delete.description:
`DELETE /v1/passkeys/{id} {current_password? | passkey? | grant?}` →
`{id, removed: true}`, once it is proved still the person
([`reauthenticate`]) — or with a `grant` this device was given for this
passkey, below. **The proof comes first**: a wrong one is `403
reauth_failed` whatever the passkey's state, and learns nothing of it.
Never the account's last way to sign in (`409 last_credential`, §3.6),
and never a passkey a current slot on the chain unlocks with (`409
unlock_on`): the page takes the slot off first (`PasskeySlotRemove`,
§4.8), so no slot is left naming a passkey nobody can sign in with — and
a chain that cannot be read is no answer (`503`). After a proof (not a
grant), that `409` carries a `grant` ([`Purpose::Removal`]: this account,
this device, this passkey, two minutes, good once): the page signs
`PasskeySlotRemove` and sends it back as `{grant}`, asking the person for
nothing twice. The chain's lock is held from the slot check to the commit,
so a `PasskeySlotSet` naming the passkey cannot land in between. Recorded
and told like every change ([`record`]). A current full device.

put.description:
`PUT /v1/password {password, current_password? | passkey?}` →
`{password: true}`: the account's password set (an account made with a
passkey has none) or changed (§3.6) — after proving it is still the
person ([`reauthenticate`]: a passkey of the account's, or the current
password where there is one). Recorded and told like every change
([`record`]): `password_set` or `password_changed`, by whether the account
had one under the lock. A current full device.

default.description: `error` is the code, `message` a sentence; some codes add fields below.

delete.description:
`DELETE /v1/rotations/{host} {nonce_hash? | requested_ms?}` (an admin;
renewals on or off): withdraw — the row goes (a committed one stays its
day). An isolated host stays `pending`: only a renewal confirmed on the
device, or its removal, clears it.

The body names what is withdrawn, so that a page cleaning up after
itself (or after an attempt nothing shows any more) never withdraws
another page's: `nonce_hash` an attempt or its staging (the hash its `PUT`
sent, the row's `nonce_hash`), `requested_ms` a `pending` mark (the row's
`requested_ms`). A row that is not the one named is left as it is: `409
rotation_in_progress` while it is another attempt or staging (one opened
on top of the named mark included), else `200 {}` — the one named is gone
already. No body, or `{}`: whatever the host has, as before there was a
body. Both fields, or anything else: `400 bad_request`.

AccountDeleted.description:
`DELETE /v1/account {confirm, current_password? | passkey?}` →
`{deleted: true, purged}`: the account and everything it stores
([`Eraser::delete`]), asked from a current full device (any device before
the account has a chain), with the account's e-mail typed out (`400
confirm_mismatch`) and proof it is still the person — a passkey of the
account's for a challenge this device was given, or the current password
(`403 reauth_required` / `reauth_failed`, as `PUT /v1/password`).
`purged: false`: it is gone for its owner, and the hub finishes erasing
it on its own.
`DELETE /v1/account`: whether the account is gone and whether its data was
purged at once (a `false` purge finishes in the background).

ApiErrorBody.description:
The error body every handler can send: `{error, message}` (some codes add
`retry_after_ms`, `key`/`limit`/`used`). `ApiError` has no `Deserialize`
and is never a success body; this is only how `ApiResult<T>` documents
its `default` response.
The error body's shape, derived: `ApiError` itself has no `Serialize` (it
is never a success body), so its `Schematic` delegates here and the
document gets the properties, required/optional as the fields are.

ChainHead.description: `GET /v1/chain`: the entries from `from` on, as hex, and the head.

seq.description: The chain's sequence, or `null` before its genesis.

Challenge.description:
A nonce for a device to sign. No bearer: what mints a session is the
device's signature over the nonce, never a token. Stateless (an HMAC over
the ids and the time), so asking stores nothing; issued whether or not the
device exists, so the answer says nothing about which ids are real.
`POST /v1/session/challenge`: the nonce to sign.

ChallengeOptions.description:
A WebAuthn ceremony's challenge and options (the options object is the
browser's own; its shape is WebAuthn's).

DeleteAccount.description:
`DELETE /v1/account`'s body: the account's e-mail typed out, and proof it
is still the person (as `PUT /v1/password` takes it).

Deletion.description: A deleted account's address hold, in days.

Disputed.description:
`POST /v1/rotations/{host}/disputes {seq, entry_hash, sig}` — no session:
the retired key's signature is the credential (§3.8 「证据：退役钥签的争议
声明」). A host whose identity key was renewed elsewhere signs, with the key
that renewal retired, a statement over that renewal (`rh/v1
rotate-dispute`, `rh_proto::chain::rotate_dispute_body`); checked with
rh-proto against the hub's chain, kept (once per renewal: sending it
again answers the same), told to the devices (`host_dispute {kind:
"disputed"}`), and — when it disputes a renewal not confirmed on the
device with none confirmed on the device after it — it isolates the host.
Decided, kept and applied under the account's chain lock, in one
transaction (Codex #6). Only a statement that verifies is charged to the
host's limit; anything else only to the sender's address (R6 re-review
N1: junk cannot use up the real host's statement).
200 `{ok: true}`; 404 `no_such_renewal`; 410 `host_removed` (stop
sending); 422 `invalid_dispute`; 429.
`POST /v1/rotations/{host}/disputes`: the statement was taken.

EnrollmentState.description:
`GET /v1/enrollments/{token}`: `waiting`/`expired`, or `proved` with the
machine's keys and the proof it sent.

KeyPut.description:
Store one keyring blob: only a current full device, each name once (the
same bytes again is a retry), only a name that ends with the device itself
and names epochs the chain has committed ([`crate::keyring`]). The blobs
are AEAD-bound to their account, machine and epochs, and every key in them
must match the chain's commitment besides; write-once names bound to their
writer keep a device from crowding out, replacing or squatting what
another writes (M2 re-review #27).
`PUT /v1/keys/{name}`: the name and whether this call stored it (the same
bytes again is a retry: `stored: false`).

turnstile.description:
The Turnstile widget's token, once the hub asked for one

MachineCopy.description: The hub's offline copy of a machine's streams.

via.description:
The relays the machine says it is signed in on, with its round trip
to each (information, never authority: §2.9).

The session device's own mailbox, a page at a time.
One unacknowledged mail.

Mailbox.description: `GET /v1/mailbox`: a page of the device's own mail.

MainDevice.description:
The account's main device as it stands: the machine and when it was set
(or cleared). `machine: None`: the account has none.

Me.description: `GET /v1/me`: the account, its devices and machines, and the chain's head.

plan.description: The plan and its usage; `null` when it could not be read.

rotations.description: Identity key renewals: policy and each host's state.

waiting.description: Hosts whose agents do not speak chain v3 yet.

MeCredentials.description: `/v1/me`'s `credentials`: whether there is a password, and how many passkeys.

MeDevice.description: One device of the account, as `GET /v1/me` lists it.

removed_ms.description: Revoked or removed from the chain; `null` for one in use or waiting.

MeRotations.description:
`/v1/me`'s `rotations`: whether renewals are on, T, and each host's state.
(The account's policy is its chain's: `SetRenewalPolicy`.)
`/v1/me`'s `rotations`: whether renewals are on, T, and each host's state.

host.description: The machine it runs on (an aggregator's host). Metadata only.

kind.description:
What the device is (local-aggregator §3.3: `"aggregator"`, a
computer's limited device). Metadata only, shown on the devices page.

replaces.description:
The device of this account it takes the place of: its browser lost
that one's keys (`GET /v1/me` says so, for the device that adds this
one to offer the old one's removal). Metadata only; an id that is not
a device of this account is kept as none.

PairingOpened.description:
A device opens a pairing for itself (one not in the chain yet, typically:
that one gets a short-lived quota, [`crate::pairings::Opener`]).
`POST /v1/pairings`: the pairing's id.

PairingPosted.description:
The initiator is a current full device; the responder is the device that
opened the pairing.
`POST /v1/pairings/{id}/messages`: the message's number in the pairing.

PasskeyList.description: `GET /v1/passkeys`: the account's passkeys and whether it has a password.

PasskeyView.description:
One passkey as the account's devices see it (`GET /v1/passkeys`). Nothing
here is a secret: the credential id is what every assertion carries, and
the page needs it to ask that very passkey for its PRF (§4.5).
One passkey, as `GET /v1/passkeys` and the add/rename routes show it.

cred_hash.description: Hex; names the chain's key slot this passkey unlocks.

unlock.description: `on` or `off`: whether this passkey unlocks a slot of the chain.

Passkeys.description: The passkey relying party the browser binds credentials to.

PasswordState.description: `PUT`/`DELETE /v1/password`: whether the account has a password now.

PlanTransfer.description:
What went through the relays in the period (what went straight between two
devices is not counted).

PlanUsage.description: What the account uses against the plan.

machines.description: `hosts`' old name, for clients from before chain v3 (one version).

PlanView.description:
`/v1/me`'s `plan`: the plan, its dates, the effective entitlements and the
usage — and `warnings`, the keys the account is near (80%) where nearing
one matters before it is met: `chain.entries` (a full chain takes only
removals and the way out: [`crate::hub::chain_caps`]).
`/v1/me`'s `plan`: the plan, its dates, the effective entitlements, the
usage and the keys it is nearing.

warnings.description: Keys the account is near (80%) where nearing one matters.

PresenceState.description:
One of the three presence states (architecture doc §5): `unknown` while
the hub cannot yet say (it restarted less than a freshness window ago and
has not heard from the machine).

Proof.description:
Proof it is still the person, as a body ([`reauthenticate`]): adding or
removing a passkey, removing the password — or, removing a passkey only,
the `grant` an earlier proof was given with `409 unlock_on` ([`remove`]).

ReauthPasskey.description: A passkey's answer to a re-authentication challenge.

RelayList.description: `GET /v1/relays`: the relays the hub knows, the account's set and limits.

agents.description: Machine id → relay id → round trip (ms), the agents' own reports.

emergency.description: Relays granted to the account in an emergency.

RelayPrefs.description:
`PATCH /v1/relays/prefs {standby?}` → `{standby}`: the account's relay
preferences, set by a current device of its chain. Not security-sensitive
(which relays carry ciphertext); a change fills or trims the set at once
([`Hub::fill_set`]) and its agents hear of it.
`PATCH /v1/relays/prefs`: the account's relay preferences.

RotationsView.description:
The account's renewals as `GET /v1/rotations` gives them.
`GET /v1/rotations`: the hub's clock, the policy, each host's state and
the disputes kept.

hosts.description: One entry per host, as `rotation_json` builds it.

SignInChange.description:
`GET /v1/me`'s `sign_in_changes`: the account's changes of the last
[`CHANGES_KEPT_MS`] up to `now`, oldest first, at most [`CHANGES_LISTED`]
(the newest), each `{id, kind, device, label, at_ms}` as
`sign_in_changed` says it.
One recent change to the account's ways to sign in, as `/v1/me` lists it.

invite.description: Required with `DROPPEN_HUB_SIGNUP=invite`; optional (and may give a plan) when open.

lang.description: The language mail is written in.

turnstile.description: The Turnstile widget's token (when Turnstile is on).

email_verified.description:
Whether the account's e-mail is verified (always `true` with
verification off).

known_client.description:
The hub's word that this client signed in to the account
([`auth::known_client_token`]): sent with its next login.

passkey.description: The passkey a passkey login used (`POST /v1/login/passkey`).

SignupConfig.description:
`GET /v1/signup/config`: what the sign-up page needs to draw its form.
Field order and `null`s match the `Json<Value>` it replaces (the open
clients read it; a missing field is a contract change). The order is
alphabetical because that `Value` came from `serde_json`'s `BTreeMap`,
and `tests/golden/single_host.txt` compares the body byte for byte.

deletion.description: How long a deleted account's address cannot sign up again.

invite_required.description: Whether an invite code is required.

passkeys.description: Passkeys' relying party, when passkeys are offered.

turnstile.description: Turnstile's widget, when it is on.

TicketRefusal.description: Why one relay got no ticket.

error.description:
`unknown` (not in the list for this account), `unavailable` (not
`up`), `limit` (the set is full) or `forbidden`.

Turnstile.description: The Turnstile widget the sign-up page renders (alphabetical, as above).

origin.description: The origin the widget's page is served on.

Verified.description:
The link's token (from the page at `/verify`, which read it from the
fragment): no session needed — the token is the proof, from any device.
`POST /v1/email/verify`: the account the link verified.

Waitlisted.description:
`POST /v1/waitlist`: `{ok: true}` whether the address was new or already
there.
